historical_record.description: The Recreation and Park Commission named the softball diamond at Glen Park in honor of Thelma Williams, for her work for youth softball in San Francisco.

Under the Glen Canyon master plan, the Recreation and Park Commission approved improving the trail up the side of the canyon, widening part of it and adding a bridge, with the work by the Conservation Corps.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved a Conservation Corps stream restoration in Glen Canyon, thinning the willows to let light reach Islais Creek so insects such as the San Francisco forktail damselfly could return; the stream once held California roach, threespine stickleback and Sacramento sucker, and possibly steelhead.

On the Glen Park Playground land the Board of Supervisors bought in 1922, a large storm sewer was laid in the bed of the creek that crossed it, and the area was filled, leveled and turfed for baseball.
